new.analysis:
Your week of Sep 21 – 27 shows no distance and no heart-rate data on any of the three planned days. Your check-in says you slept 7.5 hours, stress was low and your body felt fine, so nothing there points to a problem. I can't tell from here whether the runs were skipped or just not recorded, and that matters for how I read your consistency.

Nine days without running costs very little fitness, so this is a short step back and not a reset. The first two runs are a check that things feel the same as they did before the gap. I kept the total at about 69 minutes, roughly 10 percent above the 63 minutes you ran the week of Sep 14 – 20, so the volume stays gradual.

Every run this week stays easy, even though the build phase usually adds threshold work. You are not yet running continuously, so there is nothing to hold at threshold, and the useful build is longer run segments with shorter walks. Hard running would add risk without helping you run 5K without walking.

The week of Sep 14 – 20 is why I am watching effort. Only about half of your heart-rate time sat in zones 1 and 2 with no hard running at all. The run segments were already on the firm side of easy, and longer segments at that pace would get uncomfortable quickly.

The goal is within reach but the margin is thin. Over the next weeks the run segments grow a step at a time, the walks shrink, and one lighter week sits before race week. That path only works if the three sessions each week actually happen, so a steady week matters more than a bigger one.
